name: s5-ordering
comment: MOVE ORDERING + HISTORY SHAPING, jointly (2026-07-28, searchopt). Why this family and why SPSA rather than more screening: a 15-arm single-knob screen against pooled nodes-to-depth-13 over 120 plateau positions found that EVERY perturbation increases nodes (base sits in a shallow minimum), and the one apparent winner (QUIET_CHECK_BONUS 16384->8192, -3.0%) has a non-monotone dose response (2048 +1.3%, 4096 -3.2%, 8192 -3.0%, 12288 +2.5%), i.e. it is inside the chaos band. Single-knob screening is exhausted; interactions are all that is left, which is what SPSA is for. These 16 are ALSO the right family on priors: unlike the eval-frame pruning margins (whose blanket rescale is refuted in both directions, see docs/research/eval-frame-scale-model-2026-07-27.md S11.4), ordering weights are denominated in OUR history units and scale with OUR history value distribution, so SF's tuned values carry no guarantee. All 16 are SPSA-uncovered (param_provenance: 256/305 uncovered). Ordering is also the one lever that improves the tree WITHOUT enlarging it -- every tree-widening arm with game evidence loses (lmr30 -11.6 n=628, EVAL_SCALE 2200 -27.8, corrgate -17.1 n=406, setrigger -16.3 n=406), so the width optimum is pinned and node-neutral gains are the only ones available.
r_end_note: r_end = 0.03, copied from s2-stageA for the same reason recorded there: the 0.002 default moves ~1% of range over the iteration count this box affords and produces a null BY CONSTRUCTION. These are SF-transcribed values that have never been tuned against our history scale, so the larger step is justified. Verify any winner at 10+0.1 before pinning (screen -> verify -> bracket -> pin).
engine_note: A non-PGO tune build is CORRECT here and this is not a deviation from the standing PGO ruling: SPSA plays fixed-NODE games, both sides are the same binary, and PGO changes only speed, not the search tree. Results are bit-identical between PGO and non-PGO at fixed nodes. PGO matters for wall-clock throughput only.
c_end_note: c_end defaults to (max-min)/20 and non-float params render as int(round(v)), so a small-integer parameter goes INERT as c_k decays to c_end: QUIET_MAIN_HISTORY_WEIGHT has range 5 => c_end 0.25, and at theta=2.0 both perturbations (2.25, 1.75) round to 2. c_k runs from 2.16*c_end down to c_end (GAMMA=0.101, iters=2000), so such a dimension works early and dies late. Fix applied: the two range-5 history weights are DROPPED from SPSA -- with 6 legal values they are better screened exhaustively, and they already were (1/3/4 all worse-or-flat on fhf against a +-0.0011 null band). CAPTURE_MVV_FACTOR (range 11) keeps an explicit c_end of 1.0 so its perturbations always straddle an integer boundary. Raising c_end raises movement roughly linearly (update ~ r_end*c_end^2/c_k ~ c_end), which is intended for a coarse integer axis.
